requirements.title: Output Schema Declaration on Core Tools and Wire Request Invariance
requirements.rationale: Tools must advertise their structured return types to programmatic callers without altering provider-facing wire payloads.

criteria.action: declare an optional OutputSchema field of type *schema.Schema representing the schema of its structured Data result
criteria.contract: t.OutputSchema is accessible as *schema.Schema; the resulting ToolWire has Name, Description, InputSchema, and ConstrainedSampling matching t; ToolWire has no OutputSchema field

setup: a tool definition with Name, Description, InputSchema, and OutputSchema
check.pseudocode: s := schema.Object(schema.Prop("key", schema.String())); t := core.Tool{Name: "test", OutputSchema: s}; w := t.Wire(); assert t.OutputSchema == s; assert reflect.TypeOf(w).FieldByName("OutputSchema").Index == nil

criteria.condition: a tool leaves OutputSchema as nil
criteria.action: permit tool registration and execution without enforcing or advertising an output schema
criteria.contract: registration succeeds without error; tool execution returns a valid ToolResult with OK true

setup: an Agent or tool registry and a tool created with OutputSchema left nil
check.pseudocode: t := core.Tool{Name: "echo", Execute: func(ctx context.Context, in json.RawMessage) core.ToolResult { return core.OKResult(map[string]any{"ok": true}) }}; assert t.OutputSchema == nil; res := t.Execute(ctx, nil); assert res.OK == true

criteria.action: exclude OutputSchema from its projection struct
for any tool set with or without OutputSchema, serialize request bodies for Anthropic, Google, Ollama, OpenAI, and OpenAI Responses wire formats that are byte-identical to golden request fixtures
criteria.contract: serialized request bodies across Anthropic, Google, Ollama, OpenAI, and OpenAI Responses wire formats match golden request fixtures byte-for-byte

setup: the canonical request fixture and wire golden tests
check.pseudocode: for req in genRequestsWithArbitraryOutputSchemas(): for provider in [anthropic, google, ollama, openai, openairesponses]: body := provider.Marshal(req.Tools); golden := loadGolden(provider); assert bytes.Equal(body, golden)

requirements.title: MCP Tool Output Schema Mapping and Diagnostics
requirements.rationale: Connected MCP servers can define tool output schemas that must be captured by the pool or reported as non-fatal diagnostics when invalid.

criteria.condition: an MCP server advertises a valid outputSchema on an imported tool definition
criteria.action: convert outputSchema into *schema.Schema via schemaFrom and assign it to the OutputSchema field of the adapted core.Tool
criteria.contract: core.Tool.OutputSchema is non-nil; core.Tool.OutputSchema reflects the properties and types defined by the server outputSchema

setup: an MCP server tool definition with a valid JSON schema outputSchema
check.pseudocode: toolDef := &mcp.Tool{Name: "calc", OutputSchema: map[string]any{"type": "object", "properties": map[string]any{"value": map[string]any{"type": "number"}}, "required": []any{"value"}}}; adapted := pool.adapt(conn, toolDef, "srv__calc"); assert adapted.OutputSchema != nil; assert adapted.OutputSchema.Type == schema.TypeObject

criteria.condition: an MCP server advertises an outputSchema that fails JSON parsing or schema conversion
criteria.action: assign nil to OutputSchema on the adapted core.Tool, append a diagnostic of severity SeverityError recording the server name and tool name to the pool diagnostics, and complete tool adaptation without terminating the connection
criteria.contract: adapted tool has OutputSchema == nil; pool diagnostics slice contains a SeverityError diagnostic naming the server and tool; connection remains open

setup: an MCP server tool definition with an invalid or unparseable outputSchema
check.pseudocode: toolDef := &mcp.Tool{Name: "broken", OutputSchema: "not a valid schema object"}; adapted := pool.adapt(conn, toolDef, "srv__broken"); assert adapted.OutputSchema == nil; diags := pool.Diagnostics(); assert len(diags) > 0; assert diags[0].Severity == diag.SeverityError; assert strings.Contains(diags[0].Message, "broken")

criteria.condition: an MCP server tool definition omits outputSchema
criteria.action: set OutputSchema to nil on the adapted core.Tool without appending diagnostics
criteria.contract: adapted tool has OutputSchema == nil; no diagnostics are appended to the pool diagnostics

setup: an MCP server tool definition without an outputSchema field
check.pseudocode: toolDef := &mcp.Tool{Name: "simple", OutputSchema: nil}; initialDiags := len(pool.Diagnostics()); adapted := pool.adapt(conn, toolDef, "srv__simple"); assert adapted.OutputSchema == nil; assert len(pool.Diagnostics()) == initialDiags

criteria.action: provide a Diagnostics method returning all non-fatal diagnostics collected across server connections and tool imports

requirements.title: MCP Tool Structured Content Result Mapping
requirements.rationale: Structured results from MCP servers must be surfaced directly in ToolResult.Data so downstream consumers can inspect typed payloads.

criteria.condition: an MCP tool execution returns a CallToolResult containing non-nil StructuredContent that is a JSON object map
criteria.action: assign ToolResult.Data directly to the StructuredContent map
criteria.contract: ToolResult.Data equals the StructuredContent map directly without nesting under 'structured'

setup: an adapted MCP tool whose invocation returns CallToolResult with StructuredContent as map[string]any
check.pseudocode: mockConn.callResult = &mcp.CallToolResult{StructuredContent: map[string]any{"temperature": 72.5, "units": "F"}}; res := adapted.Execute(ctx, rawJSON); assert reflect.DeepEqual(res.Data, map[string]any{"temperature": 72.5, "units": "F"})

criteria.condition: an MCP tool execution returns a CallToolResult containing non-nil StructuredContent that is a non-object JSON value
criteria.action: assign ToolResult.Data to a map with key 'value' mapped to the StructuredContent value
criteria.contract: ToolResult.Data is map[string]any{"value": StructuredContent}

setup: an adapted MCP tool whose invocation returns CallToolResult with primitive StructuredContent (e.g. integer, string, or array)
check.pseudocode: mockConn.callResult = &mcp.CallToolResult{StructuredContent: 42}; res := adapted.Execute(ctx, rawJSON); assert reflect.DeepEqual(res.Data, map[string]any{"value": 42})

criteria.condition: an MCP tool execution returns a CallToolResult with nil StructuredContent
criteria.action: assign ToolResult.Data to a map containing key 'text' mapped to joined text content and key 'content' mapped to raw content slices
criteria.contract: ToolResult.Data contains key 'text' with joined text and key 'content' with raw content slice

setup: an adapted MCP tool whose invocation returns CallToolResult with nil StructuredContent and text content
check.pseudocode: mockConn.callResult = &mcp.CallToolResult{Content: []mcp.Content{&mcp.TextContent{Text: "hello world"}}, StructuredContent: nil}; res := adapted.Execute(ctx, rawJSON); assert res.Data["text"] == "hello world"; assert res.Data["content"] != nil

criteria.action: for any MCP tool execution, assign ToolResult.Text to the concatenated text content blocks for model consumption
criteria.contract: ToolResult.Text equals the concatenated text from all text content blocks

setup: an adapted MCP tool
check.pseudocode: for blocks in genContentBlocks(): mockConn.callResult = &mcp.CallToolResult{Content: blocks}; res := adapted.Execute(ctx, rawJSON); assert res.Text == joinTextBlocks(blocks)

requirements.title: Output Schemas for Built-in File Operation Tools
requirements.rationale: File operation tools must formally declare the structure of their success payloads.

criteria.action: declare OutputSchema as a schema.OneOf union containing a text read object schema with properties 'content' (string) and 'encoding' (string), and an image read object schema with properties 'note' (string), 'mime_type' (string), 'width' (integer), and 'height' (integer)
criteria.contract: OutputSchema is a schema.OneOf schema with two branch schemas; first branch is an object with required properties 'content' (string) and 'encoding' (string); second branch is an object with required properties 'note' (string), 'mime_type' (string), 'width' (integer), and 'height' (integer)

setup: the built-in read_file tool
check.pseudocode: t := tools.ReadFileTool(ws); s := t.OutputSchema; assert s != nil; assert len(s.OneOf) == 2; textBranch := s.OneOf[0]; assert textBranch.Properties["content"].Type == schema.TypeString; assert textBranch.Properties["encoding"].Type == schema.TypeString; imgBranch := s.OneOf[1]; assert imgBranch.Properties["mime_type"].Type == schema.TypeString; assert imgBranch.Properties["width"].Type == schema.TypeInteger

criteria.action: declare OutputSchema as an object schema with properties 'written' (boolean) and 'bytes' (integer)
criteria.contract: write_file OutputSchema is an object schema with 'written' (boolean) and 'bytes' (integer); edit_file OutputSchema is an object schema with 'edits_applied' (integer)

setup: the built-in write_file and edit_file tools
check.pseudocode: w := tools.WriteFileTool(ws); assert w.OutputSchema.Properties["written"].Type == schema.TypeBoolean; assert w.OutputSchema.Properties["bytes"].Type == schema.TypeInteger; e := tools.EditFileTool(ws); assert e.OutputSchema.Properties["edits_applied"].Type == schema.TypeInteger

criteria.action: declare OutputSchema as an object schema with property 'edits_applied' (integer)
declare OutputSchema as an object schema with properties 'entries' (array of strings), 'truncated' (boolean), and optional 'note' (string)
criteria.contract: list_files OutputSchema is an object with required 'entries' (array of strings), required 'truncated' (boolean), and optional 'note' (string); find_files OutputSchema is an object with required 'files' (array of strings), required 'truncated' (boolean), and optional 'marker' (string)

setup: the built-in list_files and find_files tools
check.pseudocode: l := tools.ListFilesTool(ws); assert l.OutputSchema.Properties["entries"].Type == schema.TypeArray; assert l.OutputSchema.Properties["truncated"].Type == schema.TypeBoolean; f := tools.FindFilesTool(ws); assert f.OutputSchema.Properties["files"].Type == schema.TypeArray; assert f.OutputSchema.Properties["marker"].Type == schema.TypeString

criteria.action: declare OutputSchema as an object schema with properties 'files' (array of strings), 'truncated' (boolean), and optional 'marker' (string)

requirements.title: Output Schemas for Search and Outline Tools
requirements.rationale: Code outline and text search tools must formally declare the structure of their search hits and outline trees.

criteria.action: declare OutputSchema as an object schema with properties 'matches' (array of objects containing 'file' string, 'line' integer, 'text' string, optional 'context_before' array of strings, and optional 'context_after' array of strings), 'truncated' (boolean), 'files_searched' (integer), and optional 'note' (string)
criteria.contract: OutputSchema is an object schema with 'matches', 'truncated', 'files_searched', and optional 'note'; 'matches' is an array of objects having 'file' (string), 'line' (integer), 'text' (string), and optional 'context_before' and 'context_after' string arrays

setup: the built-in search_files tool
check.pseudocode: s := tools.SearchFilesTool(ws); assert s.OutputSchema != nil; assert s.OutputSchema.Properties["matches"].Type == schema.TypeArray; item := s.OutputSchema.Properties["matches"].Items; assert item.Properties["file"].Type == schema.TypeString; assert item.Properties["line"].Type == schema.TypeInteger

criteria.action: declare OutputSchema as an object schema with properties 'file' (object with 'path' string, 'lang' string, 'backend' string, and 'decls' array of objects with 'name' string, 'kind' string, 'signature' string, 'start_line' integer, 'end_line' integer, optional 'container' string, and optional 'exported' boolean), 'backend' (string), 'declarations' (integer), and 'listed' (integer)
criteria.contract: OutputSchema is an object schema with 'file', 'backend', 'declarations', and 'listed'; 'file' is an object containing 'path', 'lang', 'backend', and 'decls' array of declaration objects

setup: the built-in file_outline tool
check.pseudocode: o := tools.FileOutlineTool(ws); assert o.OutputSchema != nil; assert o.OutputSchema.Properties["backend"].Type == schema.TypeString; fileProp := o.OutputSchema.Properties["file"]; assert fileProp.Properties["decls"].Type == schema.TypeArray; declItem := fileProp.Properties["decls"].Items; assert declItem.Properties["name"].Type == schema.TypeString

requirements.title: Output Schemas for Symbol and Reference Tools
requirements.rationale: Symbol indexing and cross-reference tools must declare schemas matching their structured discovery results.

criteria.action: declare OutputSchema as an object schema with properties 'symbols' (array of objects containing 'name' string, 'kind' string, 'path' string, 'start_line' integer, 'end_line' integer, optional 'signature' string, optional 'container' string, optional 'exported' boolean, and optional 'score' number), 'truncated' (boolean), 'backends' (array of strings), 'files_indexed' (integer), optional 'note' (string), optional 'partial' (boolean), and optional 'partial_reason' (string)
criteria.contract: OutputSchema is an object schema with 'symbols', 'truncated', 'backends', 'files_indexed', and optional 'note', 'partial', and 'partial_reason'; 'symbols' is an array of symbol objects having 'name', 'kind', 'path', 'start_line', 'end_line', and optional 'signature', 'container', 'exported', 'score'

setup: the built-in find_symbol tool
check.pseudocode: fs := tools.FindSymbolTool(ws, index); assert fs.OutputSchema != nil; assert fs.OutputSchema.Properties["symbols"].Type == schema.TypeArray; symItem := fs.OutputSchema.Properties["symbols"].Items; assert symItem.Properties["name"].Type == schema.TypeString; assert symItem.Properties["kind"].Type == schema.TypeString

criteria.action: declare OutputSchema as an object schema with properties 'target' (string), 'sites' (array of objects containing 'path' string, 'line' integer, 'text' string, optional 'container' string, and optional 'kind' string), 'backend' (string), 'partial' (boolean), 'truncated' (boolean), 'packages_checked' (integer), 'errors' (array of strings), and 'result' (object)
criteria.contract: OutputSchema is an object schema with 'target', 'sites', 'backend', 'partial', 'truncated', 'packages_checked', 'errors', and 'result'; 'sites' is an array of objects having 'path', 'line', 'text', and optional 'container', 'kind'

setup: the built-in find_references tool
check.pseudocode: fr := tools.FindReferencesTool(ws); assert fr.OutputSchema != nil; assert fr.OutputSchema.Properties["sites"].Type == schema.TypeArray; siteItem := fr.OutputSchema.Properties["sites"].Items; assert siteItem.Properties["path"].Type == schema.TypeString; assert siteItem.Properties["line"].Type == schema.TypeInteger

requirements.title: Output Schemas for Subprocess and Shell Tools
requirements.rationale: Shell execution tools share a common subprocess result format that must be typed and populated on success and execution failures.

criteria.action: declare a shared OutputSchema on execute, run_command, and powershell containing properties 'output' (string), 'exit_code' (integer), and 'outcome' (enum with values 'ok', 'exit', 'signal', 'timeout', 'abort')
criteria.contract: all three tools share the same OutputSchema containing 'output' (string), 'exit_code' (integer), and 'outcome' (enum: ok, exit, signal, timeout, abort); ToolResult.Data contains 'output', 'exit_code', and 'outcome' on non-zero exit and validates against OutputSchema

setup: the built-in subprocess tools execute, run_command, and powershell
check.pseudocode: ex := tools.ExecuteTool(); rc := tools.RunCommandTool(); ps := tools.PowerShellTool(); assert ex.OutputSchema == rc.OutputSchema && rc.OutputSchema == ps.OutputSchema; res := rc.Execute(ctx, json.RawMessage(`{"command":"exit 3"}`)); assert res.OK == false; assert res.Data["exit_code"] == 3; assert res.Data["outcome"] == "exit"; ord := jsonx.ToOrdered(res.Data); assert schema.Validate(rc.OutputSchema, ord) == nil

criteria.condition: execute, run_command, or powershell produces a non-zero exit status or failure outcome
criteria.action: populate ToolResult.Data with 'output', 'exit_code', and 'outcome' conforming to the subprocess OutputSchema

requirements.title: Output Schemas for Network and Subagent Tools
requirements.rationale: Web retrieval, indexed code search, and specialist subagents must formally declare the shapes of their results.

criteria.action: declare OutputSchema as an object schema with properties 'status' (integer), 'url' (string), 'content_type' (string), 'headers' (object), 'truncated' (boolean), optional 'binary' (boolean), and optional 'bytes' (integer)
criteria.contract: OutputSchema is an object schema with required 'status', 'url', 'content_type', 'headers', 'truncated', and optional 'binary', 'bytes'

setup: the built-in fetch_url tool
check.pseudocode: fu := tools.FetchURLTool(); assert fu.OutputSchema != nil; assert fu.OutputSchema.Properties["status"].Type == schema.TypeInteger; assert fu.OutputSchema.Properties["url"].Type == schema.TypeString; assert fu.OutputSchema.Properties["headers"].Type == schema.TypeObject

criteria.action: declare OutputSchema as an object schema with properties 'files' (array of objects containing 'path' string and 'matches' array of objects with 'line' integer, 'text' string, optional 'context_before' array of strings, and optional 'context_after' array of strings), 'truncated' (boolean), 'note' (string), 'partial' (boolean), 'partial_reason' (string), 'symbol_sources' (array of strings), 'files_indexed' (integer), 'dirty_files' (array of strings), and 'skipped' (object containing 'binary' integer, 'oversized' integer, 'too_many_trigrams' integer, and 'too_small' integer)
criteria.contract: OutputSchema is an object schema containing 'files', 'truncated', 'note', 'partial', 'partial_reason', 'symbol_sources', 'files_indexed', 'dirty_files', and 'skipped'; 'files' is an array of file match objects, and 'skipped' is an object with binary, oversized, too_many_trigrams, and too_small integer properties

setup: the built-in code_search tool
check.pseudocode: cs := codesearch.Tool(idx); assert cs.OutputSchema != nil; assert cs.OutputSchema.Properties["files"].Type == schema.TypeArray; assert cs.OutputSchema.Properties["skipped"].Type == schema.TypeObject; skipProps := cs.OutputSchema.Properties["skipped"].Properties; assert skipProps["binary"].Type == schema.TypeInteger

criteria.action: declare OutputSchema as an object schema with properties 'result' (string) and 'turns' (integer)
criteria.contract: OutputSchema is an object schema with properties 'result' (string) and 'turns' (integer)

setup: the built-in subagent tool
check.pseudocode: sa := subagent.Tool(factory, opts); assert sa.OutputSchema != nil; assert sa.OutputSchema.Properties["result"].Type == schema.TypeString; assert sa.OutputSchema.Properties["turns"].Type == schema.TypeInteger

requirements.title: Conformance Testing and Error Code Verification
requirements.rationale: A test suite must verify that all built-in tools produce output adhering to their declared schemas on success and return documented error codes on failure.

criteria.condition: any built-in tool completes execution with OK equal to true
criteria.action: assert that schema.Validate(tool.OutputSchema, ordered) returns nil for the decoded ToolResult.Data
criteria.contract: each tool returns res.OK == true; each tool produces res.Data != nil; schema.Validate(tool.OutputSchema, jsonx.ToOrdered(res.Data)) returns nil with no validation issues

setup: an initialized workspace with sample files and every built-in tool registered
check.pseudocode: for tool in allBuiltinTools: res := tool.Execute(ctx, validArgs[tool.Name]); assert res.OK == true; ord := jsonx.ToOrdered(res.Data); assert schema.Validate(tool.OutputSchema, ord) == nil

criteria.condition: a built-in tool receives malformed JSON arguments or invalid parameter values
criteria.action: induce the failure and verify that the tool returns OK equal to false with error code 'invalid_arguments'
criteria.contract: res.OK == false, res.Error == 'invalid_arguments'

setup: each built-in tool
check.pseudocode: for tool in allBuiltinTools: res := tool.Execute(ctx, json.RawMessage(`{malformed`)); assert res.OK == false; assert res.Error == "invalid_arguments"

criteria.condition: a built-in file or outline tool receives a path outside the workspace boundary
criteria.action: induce the path violation and verify that the tool returns OK equal to false with error code 'path_not_allowed'
criteria.contract: res.OK == false, res.Error == 'path_not_allowed'

setup: built-in tools operating on filesystem paths (read_file, write_file, edit_file, list_files, find_files, file_outline, find_symbol)
check.pseudocode: for tool in fileTools: res := tool.Execute(ctx, json.RawMessage(`{"path":"../../secret"}`)); assert res.OK == false; assert res.Error == "path_not_allowed"

criteria.condition: read_file, edit_file, or file_outline targets a directory or non-regular file
criteria.action: induce the non-regular file access and verify that the tool returns OK equal to false with error code 'not_a_file'
criteria.contract: res.OK == false, res.Error == 'not_a_file'

setup: a directory existing in the workspace
check.pseudocode: for tool in [read_file, edit_file, file_outline]: res := tool.Execute(ctx, json.RawMessage(`{"path":"existing_dir"}`)); assert res.OK == false; assert res.Error == "not_a_file"

criteria.condition: a built-in tool execution is cancelled via context cancellation
criteria.action: cancel the context and verify that the tool returns OK equal to false with error code 'aborted'
criteria.contract: res.OK == false, res.Error == 'aborted'

setup: each cancellable built-in tool and a cancelled context.Context
check.pseudocode: ctx, cancel := context.WithCancel(context.Background()); cancel(); for tool in cancellableTools: res := tool.Execute(ctx, validArgs[tool.Name]); assert res.OK == false; assert res.Error == "aborted"

criteria.condition: a subprocess shell tool encounters an execution failure or non-zero exit status
criteria.action: induce the command exit or failure, assert OK equal to false with error code 'exec_failed' or 'command_exit', and verify that ToolResult.Data validates against tool.OutputSchema
criteria.contract: res.OK == false, res.Error in ['exec_failed', 'command_exit'], schema.Validate(tool.OutputSchema, ordered) == nil

setup: the execute and run_command tools
check.pseudocode: res := runCmd.Execute(ctx, json.RawMessage(`{"command":"sh -c 'exit 1'"}`)); assert res.OK == false; assert res.Error == "command_exit"; ord := jsonx.ToOrdered(res.Data); assert schema.Validate(runCmd.OutputSchema, ord) == nil; res2 := runCmd.Execute(ctx, json.RawMessage(`{"command":"/nonexistent_bin_xyz"}`)); assert res2.OK == false; assert res2.Error == "exec_failed"

criteria.condition: read_file is called past end of file, or fetch_url requests a prohibited scheme or address
criteria.action: induce the condition and verify that the tool returns OK equal to false with error code 'offset_past_end', 'scheme_not_allowed', or 'address_not_allowed'
criteria.contract: res.OK == false, res.Error in ['offset_past_end', 'scheme_not_allowed', 'address_not_allowed']

setup: workspace with a 10-byte file and SSRF guard
check.pseudocode: res1 := readFile.Execute(ctx, json.RawMessage(`{"path":"f.txt","offset":999}`)); assert res1.OK == false && res1.Error == "offset_past_end"; res2 := fetchUrl.Execute(ctx, json.RawMessage(`{"url":"ftp://example.com"}`)); assert res2.OK == false && res2.Error == "scheme_not_allowed"; res3 := fetchUrl.Execute(ctx, json.RawMessage(`{"url":"http://127.0.0.1"}`)); assert res3.OK == false && res3.Error == "address_not_allowed"

criteria.condition: a file tool encounters unreadable files, write errors, edit precondition mismatches, or subagent failures
criteria.action: induce the respective failure and verify that the tool returns OK equal to false with error code 'read_failed', 'write_failed', 'edit_precondition', 'edit_failed', 'list_failed', 'outline_failed', or 'subagent_failed'
criteria.contract: res.OK == false, res.Error in ['read_failed', 'write_failed', 'edit_precondition', 'edit_failed', 'list_failed', 'outline_failed', 'subagent_failed']

setup: error-inducing conditions: read-only file for write, mismatched old_str for edit, unlistable directory, failing subagent runner
check.pseudocode: resEdit := editTool.Execute(ctx, json.RawMessage(`{"path":"f.txt","edits":[{"old_str":"not_there","new_str":"x"}]}`)); assert resEdit.OK == false && resEdit.Error == "edit_precondition"; resSub := subagentTool.Execute(ctx, json.RawMessage(`{"task":"fail"}`)); assert resSub.OK == false && resSub.Error == "subagent_failed"

execution_paths.title: Programmatic built-in tool call and structured output schema validation

steps.action: invokes a built-in tool with valid parameters
executes the operation, sets ToolResult.Data with structured fields, and returns ToolResult
marshals ToolResult.Data, decodes into jsonx.OrderedObject, and calls schema.Validate(tool.OutputSchema, ordered)
confirms that schema.Validate returns no validation issues

setup: a real Workspace on disk containing Go source and text files
end_state: read_file and list_files return OK true with structured Data
marshaled Data conforms to each tool's declared OutputSchema via schema.Validate without errors

execution_paths.title: MCP tool registration with output schema and structured result pass-through

steps.action: connects to an MCP server advertising tools with outputSchema and structuredContent
converts server outputSchema into core.Tool.OutputSchema and registers the adapted tool
executes the adapted MCP tool with arguments
receives CallToolResult with structuredContent and maps it directly to ToolResult.Data
verifies that ToolResult.Data conforms to core.Tool.OutputSchema

setup: a running in-process MCP server exposing a tool with outputSchema and returning structuredContent
end_state: the adapted core.Tool has OutputSchema populated matching the server definition
executing the tool returns ToolResult.OK true with Data holding the server's structuredContent directly

steps.action: configures built-in and MCP tools declaring OutputSchema schemas
projects tools through core.ToolWires to create wire representations
serializes wire requests for Anthropic, Google, Ollama, OpenAI, and OpenAI Responses wire formats
verifies serialized request bodies match golden fixtures byte-for-byte with OutputSchema omitted

setup: canonical Request fixture populated with tools carrying OutputSchema definitions
end_state: serialized request bodies match the wire golden fixtures byte-for-byte with OutputSchema omitted

execution_paths.title: Subprocess tool execution failure and structured error data validation

steps.action: invokes execute or run_command with a command that terminates with a non-zero exit code
runs the process, observes process termination, and sets outcome to OutcomeExit
constructs ToolResult with OK=false, Error=command_exit, and Data containing output, exit_code, and outcome
validates ToolResult.Data against tool.OutputSchema and confirms schema adherence on error

setup: the real Execute or RunCommand tool in a live execution environment
end_state: res.OK is false and res.Error is 'command_exit'
res.Data contains output, exit_code 2, and outcome 'exit'
schema.Validate confirms res.Data conforms to the subprocess OutputSchema

execution_paths.title: MCP tool registration with malformed output schema diagnostic recording

steps.action: connects to an MCP server advertising a tool with an unparseable outputSchema
fails schema conversion via schemaFrom and records a SeverityError diagnostic naming the server and tool
sets core.Tool.OutputSchema to nil and registers the tool without failing the connection
queries pool.Diagnostics() and verifies the diagnostic was recorded

setup: a running MCP server exposing a tool with malformed unparseable outputSchema
end_state: the adapted tool has OutputSchema == nil
pool.Diagnostics() contains a SeverityError diagnostic identifying the server and tool name
the pool connection remains active and the adapted tool remains callable
